package_info.package_versions: All versions distributed via online panels and third-party websites
package_info.why_malicious: The package is designed to lock the device screen by abusing SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification services, displaying a persistent ransom note that blocks user access and coerces payment. It employs advanced obfuscation and loads its main payload dynamically in memory to evade detection and hinder analysis.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on app launch or after installation)
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (e.g., MainActivity.java or equivalent entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code requests the SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission, creates a ransom note view, and overlays it on top of all other UI elements, blocking user interaction and access to the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW to create a persistent, non-dismissible overlay that blocks all user input is highly atypical and indicative of ransomware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps may use SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW for brief alerts or floating widgets, but not to lock the entire device and demand ransom.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Chat heads in messaging apps or accessibility overlays for visually impaired users, which do not block all input or demand payment.
key_indicators: Blocks all user input and navigation

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial execution or on specific event)
execution_context.file_location: Obfuscated main payload in memory, invoked via gvmthHtyN.XoqF()

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: gvmthHtyN.XoqF(appObj, configurations); // Obfuscated method call to trigger main payload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code invokes an obfuscated method to dynamically load and execute the main ransomware payload from memory, enabling further malicious actions such as device lockout and ransom note display.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated class and method names combined with dynamic in-memory payload loading are techniques commonly used to evade static analysis and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not obfuscate core logic to this extent or load their main functionality dynamically from memory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or anti-tamper solutions may use obfuscation, but not for user-facing core logic or to lock devices.
key_indicators: Obfuscated class and method names (e.g., gvmthHtyN.XoqF)
Dynamic in-memory execution of main payload
Absence of descriptive code in static files

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses accessibility services to monitor for system dialog events indicating attempts to dismiss the overlay, and immediately re-displays the ransom note to maintain persistent lockout.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessibility services are being exploited to enforce malicious UI behavior and prevent the user from dismissing the ransom overlay.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Accessibility services are intended to assist users with disabilities, not to enforce persistent overlays or block recovery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility features for screen readers or input assistance, which do not prevent user recovery or enforce overlays.
key_indicators: Monitoring accessibility events for system dialogs
Immediate re-application of ransom overlay upon dismissal attempt

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses notification services to monitor for system notifications and suppress or override legitimate alerts, preventing the user from receiving help or system warnings.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Suppressing system notifications is a technique to prevent user awareness of security or recovery options and hinder remediation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Notification listeners are intended for user convenience, not to suppress critical system or security notifications.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Notification management apps may organize or mute notifications, but do not suppress security or system alerts.
key_indicators: Suppression of system or security notifications
Notification listener used to block recovery-related alerts

attack_chain.action: App is installed and requests SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation for device lockout and ransom note display

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated main payload is loaded and executed in memory.
Ransom note overlay is displayed, blocking all user input and access.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is locked out and prompted to pay ransom

attack_chain.action: Accessibility and notification services are abused to prevent overlay dismissal and suppress system alerts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent lockout and reduced chance of user recovery

behavioral_signatures: Requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions in combination
Displaying persistent, non-dismissible overlays that block all user input
Presence of obfuscated code with meaningless class and method names (e.g., gvmthHtyN.XoqF)
Dynamic loading and execution of main payload from memory
Suppression or overriding of system notifications via notification listener
Abuse of accessibility events to re-apply overlays and prevent user recovery
file_indicators: APK files containing obfuscated class or method names such as gvmthHtyN or XoqF
Presence of code that requests SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions together
Unusual use of accessibility and notification service handlers to enforce overlays or suppress alerts
network_indicators: May contact C2 servers for ransom payment instructions (typical for ransomware, but not explicitly mentioned in report)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that request SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, accessibility, and notification permissions together. Flag apps that display persistent overlays blocking all input. Analyze APKs for obfuscated code and dynamic payload loading (e.g., methods like gvmthHtyN.XoqF). Detect suppression of system notifications and abuse of accessibility events to enforce overlays. Use behavioral analysis to identify apps that lock the screen and demand ransom, and correlate with file and runtime indicators for high-confidence detection.
